questions.question: Q: Name the four main layers of the Earth from the surface inward.
questions.correctAnswer: Crust, mantle, outer core, inner core.

questions.question: Q: How do seismic waves provide evidence for Earth's internal structure?
questions.correctAnswer: P-waves travel through all layers (solids and liquids) but refract at boundaries. S-waves cannot pass through the liquid outer core, creating a shadow zone. The patterns of wave refraction and shadow zones reveal the depth and state of each layer.

questions.question: Q: Why is the inner core solid despite temperatures of ~5,500 degrees C?
questions.correctAnswer: The immense pressure at that depth raises the melting point of iron and nickel above the actual temperature, keeping it solid.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Earth's Structure & Composition

questions.question: Q: What is the difference between continental and oceanic crust?
questions.correctAnswer: Continental crust is thicker (30-70 km), less dense (~2.7 g/cm3), and granitic in composition. Oceanic crust is thinner (5-10 km), denser (~3.0 g/cm3), and basaltic.

questions.question: Q: What generates Earth's magnetic field?
questions.correctAnswer: Convection currents in the liquid iron-nickel outer core, acting as a geodynamo, generate Earth's magnetic field.
